newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil shrs end up after seesaw trade on Telebras.
newsitem.headline: Brazil shrs end up after seesaw trade on Telebras.

text.p: Brazilian stocks seesawed to end slightly higher on late buying of Telebras, though volume failed to rise as expected, brokers said.
The Sao Paulo bourse's Bovespa index .BVSP of the 49 most traded shares closed up 0.26 percent at 66,585 points. Turnover was 270.3 million reais ($263.7 million), below Friday's 380 million reais.

Analysts said expectations over the publication of the bid terms for the privatization of Band B cellular services this week and optimism over Telebras' nine-month earnings due to be released soon contributed to boosting market sentiment.
Telebras preferred rose 1.02 percent to 79 reais, while the company's common shares gained 0.16 percent, ending at 64.10 reais.
Traders said two factors could affect trade on Tuesday: the release of export figures for October and the U.S. presidential elections.

The Industry and Commerce Ministry is due to release export data for October and analysts will be looking for confirmation of market estimates that Brazil's trade deficit will be lower than previously expected.
Analysts now predict the country's trade gap will be around $700-$800 million, well below previous estimates of up to $1.5 billion.
Among other blue chips, state power utility Eletrobras firm Petrobras dropped 0.54 percent to end at 133.50 reais.

TAM preferred shares ended at 52.60 reais, off 2.59 percent. The company's stock has fallen 19 percent since one of its Fokker-100 aircraft crashed in Sao Paulo, killing at least 98 people last Thursday.
